summary: Tissa Rajapatirana (1933–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1966–1974) under Jan Willem de Jong and later held an attested post there in 1988.

Tista Biswas is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Subuddhi Charan Goswami. In 2026, Biswas was attested as Sir William Jones Research Fellow in Sanskritic Studies at the Asiatic Society.
Tiziana Pontillo (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
Todd A. Gibson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1991).

Todd T. Lewis (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Columbia University, he was attested at the College of the Holy Cross from 1996, serving as a named professor by 2016–2017.

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Geshe degree at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Kim Plofker and under doctoral supervisor David Pingree in 2008.

Tokio Takata (born 1949) is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, later holding professorships at Kyoto University (1997–2014) and Fudan University (2016–2022).

Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa and Kyoto universities, and under Kodo Sawaki. He was a professor at Komazawa University (1949–1987) and taught at Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjiro Takakusu. He held teaching posts at Fukui Normal School, Fujishima High School, and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Freiburg, and under Kitaro Nishida and Martin Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi, Kyoto, and Ryukoku universities, and was president of Kyoto University of Education.
Tom De Rauw is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Ann Heirman. By 2026, he held an AAP post at Ghent University.

Tom Ginsburg (born 1968) works in law, political science, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of California, Berkeley (~1985–1999), he taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) before joining the University of Chicago around 2008.

Tom Tillemans (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Jacques May (~1978–1984) and served as professor of Buddhist studies at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018).
Tomohiro Manabe specializes in Indology and philosophy. He taught as a lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2020) and became an associate professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Tomoko Makidono is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She held a research post at Minobusan University (attested 2015) and was a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Tomoko Masuzawa is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale, and UC Santa Barbara, and held faculty appointments at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–1999) and the University of Michigan (1999).
Tomomichi Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held academic posts at Otani University, attested as a lecturer in 2012 and as a professor in 2026.
Tomoyasu Oshima is an Indologist who studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a part-time lecturer post at Kyoto University in 2012.
Tomoyuki Komine (born 1971) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and was attested as a part-time lecturer there in 2015.
